items.headline: Scheduled prompts are one of the most practical and underused Microsoft Copilot features
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot now allows users to schedule prompts to run automatically at set times and frequencies, eliminating the need to remember recurring tasks. Common use cases include daily news digests, weekly project summaries, and Friday afternoon email prioritization. Each scheduled prompt runs up to 15 times over roughly three months before requiring renewal, serving as a built-in quarterly workflow review.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's AI Discovery and Assessment Workshops should integrate this feature as a practical adoption accelerator for Microsoft clients. Scheduled prompts directly support our 5-Phase methodology's 'Controlled Execution' phase by automating repetitive AI workflows without requiring custom development. Sales and delivery teams should demo this feature in Dynamics 365 and M365 engagements to showcase tangible time savings and reduce change management friction.

items.headline: Microsoft Build 2026 introduces GPU-acceleration directly into Fabric Data Warehouse
items.summary: Microsoft announced at Build 2026 that Fabric Data Warehouse becomes the first fully managed data warehouse to offer GPU acceleration built directly into the platform. Work IQ APIs reach general availability on June 16, enabling agents to access business context from email, calendar, meetings, and line-of-business systems. Azure HorizonDB, a next-generation PostgreSQL database, combines transactional data, vector search, and AI capabilities into a single platform for AI applications.

items.headline: From Radiology to Drug Discovery, Survey Reveals AI Is Delivering Clear Return on Investment in Healthcare
items.summary: NVIDIA's 2026 State of AI in Healthcare and Life Sciences survey shows 70% of healthcare organizations now actively deploy AI, up from 63% in 2024. Medical technology companies report 57% cite measurable returns from AI-assisted radiology, while pharma and biotech firms see 46% achieving ROI in drug discovery. A full 85% of executives report AI is helping increase revenue, while 80% report cost reductions, with 46% planning AI spending increases exceeding 10%.

items.headline: KPMG pulls report on AI usage due to apparent hallucinations
items.summary: KPMG withdrew its report 'Redefining excellence in the age of agentic AI' after multiple organizations disputed claims about their AI deployments. GPTZero found that only 5 of 45 citations pointed to real sources, while 40 titles were fabricated. UBS, UK's NHS, Swiss Federal Railways, and Transport for London all stated the report's claims about their AI usage were untrue or misleading. KPMG removed the report while conducting an investigation.

KPMG's reputation damage demonstrates why enterprises need governance playbooks and disciplined AI deployment partners, not just tool access. Use this as a battle card in Financial Services conversations where CMMI and SOC 2 matter. Frame it as validation for why our governance frameworks and AI Readiness Assessments exist before any production deployment.

items.headline: Colorado AI Act amended and effective date delayed to January 1, 2027
items.summary: On May 14, 2026, Colorado Governor Polis signed SB 189, revising the state's AI law and delaying the effective date from June 30, 2026 to January 1, 2027. The revised Act scales back original requirements, eliminating the duty of care to prevent algorithmic discrimination, deployer risk management obligations, and impact assessments. The new framework focuses on disclosure and transparency, requiring deployers to notify consumers when automated decision-making affects consequential decisions and provide meaningful human review of adverse outcomes.
items.levelshiftAngle: While Colorado scaled back compliance requirements, the revision still mandates transparency and human review for AI decisions affecting employment, housing, healthcare, and education—sectors where LevelShift operates. The January 2027 deadline gives clients a six-month runway to implement disclosure systems and human-in-the-loop workflows. Our governance playbooks and 5-Phase methodology already address these transparency requirements.
